messages.text: [FIRING:1] KubeJobFailed (namespace=payouts cluster=prod-us-east severity=warning)

replies.text: huh. one of the transfer submit jobs just failed
provider timeout? checking the job payload

messages.text: seeing timeout on submit. looks like the job got far enough to POST, then hung waiting for response.

replies.text: do we know if it actually reached the payment provider or just died client side?

messages.text: not sure yet. i'm going to retry one failed job from `payouts` and watch the provider ref.

replies.text: ok but only one, let's not fan this out until we know what's happening

messages.text: retry done. weirdly it submitted again, new provider ref. that's not great.

replies.text: wait, new ref as in new transfer? or same one with a different local id?
new transfer. i'm checking a second creator now to see if it's the same pattern

messages.text: if the first one already made it through, we may be double-paying. can we stop retries for the batch?

replies.text: agreed, pausing manual retries until we know what keying is doing

messages.text: i've got 2 creators now with 2 provider refs each. both from the retried path. pausing payouts.

replies.text: calling it out loud, do not retry anything else

messages.text: INC-1944 declared by @nd. Sev2. Duplicate payouts suspected during monthly batch. Use this channel for coordination.

replies.text: ok, incident declared

messages.text: pulling payout request rows for the affected batch. i want to compare original submit metadata vs retry metadata.

replies.text: i'm in the app too, checking the retry path code path and the job args

messages.text: can somebody confirm whether the provider timeout happened before or after the transfer was accepted? that's the key question.

replies.text: for at least one creator, provider accepted the first submit. our worker just didn't get the response in time

messages.text: found it. the retry path is minting a fresh idempotency key, not reusing the original payout identity.

replies.text: yeah, that would explain the duplicate refs

messages.text: i've got 8 creators with duplicate transfer refs so far. still counting.

replies.text: same. some are probably already final at the provider side, so we need to treat this as real money movement, not just logs

messages.text: should we freeze the rest of the batch and build the affected creator list first? i don't want more retries while we're still sorting this out.

replies.text: yes. no more retries. i can script the duplicate extraction from payouts data

messages.text: reconciliation is showing duplicate transfer refs for multiple creators. this is real, not a logging artifact.

replies.text: how many do we have?
looking like a full list of 14. still verifying one by one

messages.text: pausing payout processing now. i'll keep the queue from moving until we know exactly what got duplicated.

replies.text: thanks. i'm going through the retry workflow with jh

messages.text: confirmed. retry path generates a different idempotency key every time. the key is tied to execution context, not creator+month.

replies.text: ugh. that's the bug.
so the provider did exactly what it was told

messages.text: duplicate list is final at 14 creators. sending the names into our tracker now and starting recovery planning.

replies.text: copy. i'll keep the data pulls going for transfer refs and timestamps

messages.text: we've got the recoverable set separated. starting reversals for the ones the provider can still unwind.

replies.text: i'll stay on verification and make sure no one flips the batch back on early

messages.text: first few reversals landed cleanly. keeping the same reconciliation sheet updated as we go.

replies.text: good. i'm watching for any partials or odd statuses

messages.text: 11 reversals recovered successfully. 3 still pending provider response / not recoverable yet.

replies.text: ok, keep pushing on the remaining 3. if they don't come back we need finance in the loop

messages.text: the last 3 are not recoverable. amounts total 4,860.00 USD. flagging for write-off and moving on.

replies.text: copy. that's the line we needed to close

messages.text: hotfix is in place in `payouts` now, and the guard to persist the payout identity across retries is holding in checks.

replies.text: i'm doing one more pass on the manual retry path before we unpause

messages.text: verification looks good. retry path now reuses the original creator/month key, and the manual approval checklist is in the runbook.

replies.text: ok, no more open questions from my side

messages.text: payout queue resumed after checking the hotfix and the safeguards. thanks both.
